proof_nl: Let x be any real number. Set m = floor(x). By the defining property of the floor function, m is an integer with m <= x < m + 1. Define f = x - m. Then f >= 0, since x >= m, and f < 1, since x < m + 1. By the standard definition of the fractional part, frac(x) = x - floor(x) = x - m = f. Therefore x = m + f = floor(x) + frac(x), and also 0 <= frac(x) < 1. Since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for every real number x.
